title: AI-Powered Dynamic Mental Health Monitoring and Distress Prediction System for Victims of Atrocities
org: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE)
department: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment
description:
• Background Victims of atrocities frequently experience prolonged psychological distress after complaint registration due to threats, intimidation, repeated court appearances, delays in investigation and trial, social ostracism, economic hardship, and rehabilitation challenges.Existing mechanisms focus primarily on legal and financial support and do not provide continuous monitoring of victim well-being.
• Problem Statement Develop an AI-based Dynamic Mental Health Monitoring and Distress Prediction System that continuously monitors and predicts psychological distress among victims and complainants registered through NHAA (14566), the Integrated Portal, chatbot, mobile application, IVRS, or other approved communication channels throughout the investigation,trial, rehabilitation, and compensation process.
• Expected Solution The system should:
• Conduct periodic interactions with victims through chatbot, IVRS calls, SMS, mobile applications, web portal, or helpline follow-up mechanisms.
• Analyse voice, text, behavioural responses, and engagement patterns using NLP, Sentiment Analysis, and Emotion AI.
• Generate a Dynamic Distress Score and longitudinal trend analysis.
• Predict escalation of psychological distress before a crisis situation emerges.
• Trigger alerts to counsellors, district authorities, and designated officials when predefined risk thresholds are crossed.
• Recommend appropriate interventions such as counselling, medical treatment, witness protection, relocation support, financial assistance, legal aid, or rehabilitation measures.
• Provide dashboards at district, State, and national levels for monitoring vulnerable victims and high-risk cases.
• Ensure explainable AI, privacy protection, data security, and compliance with applicable legal and ethical standards.
• Expected Outcomes
• Continuous monitoring of victim well-being.
• Early detection and prevention of mental health crises.
• Timely deployment of counselling and rehabilitation services.
• Strengthened victim confidence in the justice delivery system.
• Evidence-based decision-making for policymakers and administrators.
• Improved coordination among welfare, counselling, and law-enforcement agencies.
• Innovation Components
• Emotion AI
• Voice Stress Analytics
• Sentiment Analysis
• Predictive Risk Modelling
• Multilingual Conversational AI
• Explainable AI
• Automated Case Prioritisation
• Real-Time Risk Alerts
• Priority Use Cases
• Victims of rape and gang rape.
• Victims of murder, grievous hurt, and arson.
• Witnesses facing intimidation or threats.
• Families affected by caste-based violence.
Beneficiaries receiving relief, compensation, rehabilitation, and protection under the provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, nlp, predictive applied to a medtech / biotech / healthtech problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (5/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within MedTech / BioTech / HealthTech. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on real-time, compliance. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 24/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: AI-Powered Dynamic Mental Health Monitoring and Distress Prediction System for Victims of Atrocities

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that checks in with victims over time, through the long, often difficult investigation and trial process, and flags when someone's distress is genuinely escalating, so support can reach them before a crisis, not just after a complaint is filed.
overview.why_it_matters: The support process for atrocity victims currently focuses on legal and financial help, with no ongoing check on how someone is actually coping through months or years of proceedings. Continuous, caring follow-up can catch a decline before it becomes a crisis.
pain_points: Victims experience prolonged psychological distress from threats, delays, and social ostracism after registering a complaint.
Existing mechanisms focus on legal/financial support with no continuous well-being monitoring.
No system currently predicts escalating distress across the long investigation-to-rehabilitation timeline.
overview.background: Atrocity victims face prolonged psychological distress throughout investigation, trial, and rehabilitation, but no system currently monitors their ongoing well-being or predicts escalating distress over this extended period.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI system conducting periodic check-ins (chatbot, IVRS, SMS) and analyzing voice, text, and behavioral engagement patterns to generate a longitudinal Dynamic Distress Score and predict escalating risk.
expected_solution: Periodic, low-friction check-in mechanism across multiple channels.
Longitudinal distress tracking and trend analysis.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Longitudinal, multi-channel distress tracking with predictive escalation flagging over a months-to-years timeline is genuinely more sophisticated than a single-point assessment, and comes with correspondingly higher responsibility.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Combines periodic multi-channel engagement, NLP/sentiment analysis, and time-series distress modeling, real technical breadth on top of the same ethical seriousness as SIH26093.

competitive_landscape.note: Same extremely sensitive domain as SIH26093, very few teams will engage, and fewer still should attempt it without real care.

innovation.note: Longitudinal, multi-channel, predictive distress tracking over an extended real-world timeline is genuinely sophisticated.

invention.note: Combines engagement design, multimodal analysis, and time-series prediction, substantial technical breadth.

technical_feasibility.note: No population-specific validation data exists; longitudinal tracking over a real timeline can't be demonstrated at hackathon scale, only prototyped conceptually.

impact_and_benefits.note: Potentially significant if it helps catch escalating crisis early, but the same real-harm risks as SIH26093 apply, amplified by the longitudinal, ongoing-relationship nature of this tool.

architecture.note: Multi-channel check-in system plus longitudinal analysis plus escalation logic, real architectural depth around a fundamentally human-safety-critical core.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick only with the same non-negotiable framing as SIH26093, human-in-the-loop, mandatory escalation, no autonomous crisis decisions. This one adds a further responsibility: check-in cadence and tone must never feel intrusive, surveillant, or re-traumatizing to someone already carrying significant distress.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Addresses a real, currently unaddressed gap, ongoing well-being support through a genuinely long, hard process that current mechanisms don't monitor at all.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: A poorly-designed check-in cadence or tone could itself feel surveillant or re-traumatizing to someone already vulnerable, and a missed or mishandled escalation of genuine crisis risk is a severe, real-world failure mode, not a demo bug.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Design the check-in experience itself with real care, consent-based, opt-out-friendly, warm in tone, not clinical or interrogative, and build the escalation-to-human pathway as the actual centerpiece of the system, with the AI analysis serving that pathway, not replacing it.

idea_0_4: Design your check-in experience with real care: consent-based, warm tone, easy opt-out, and explicitly build the human-escalation pathway as the system's core, not an add-on.
Research general (non-population-specific) longitudinal mental-health check-in and distress-monitoring design patterns responsibly.
Split: one person on the check-in/engagement design, one on the longitudinal analysis and trend logic, with shared team ownership of the escalation-safety design.
prototype_4_22: Build the periodic check-in mechanism (chatbot/SMS-style) with a genuinely warm, non-clinical tone.
Build longitudinal distress-trend analysis from check-in responses over a simulated timeline.
Build the escalation-flagging logic and, critically, the explicit human-handoff pathway for it.
integration_22_30: Connect check-in, trend analysis, and escalation into one coherent system over a simulated multi-check-in timeline.
Test with clearly synthetic, appropriately-sensitive scenarios showing both a stable trend and an escalating one.
Confirm the escalation pathway triggers unambiguously and immediately for the escalating scenario.
polish_30_36: Polish the check-in interaction for genuine warmth and respect, this is not a generic survey UI.
Rehearse presenting this with real seriousness, leading with the human-safety design, not technical sophistication.
Prepare to discuss consent, opt-out, and data privacy explicitly, given how sensitive this data is.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demonstrate a simulated escalating-distress scenario over your check-in timeline and show the system correctly, immediately routing it to a human escalation path, that safety-first design, demonstrated concretely, is what should earn credibility here, not the sophistication of the underlying model.

strengths: Addresses a genuine, currently unaddressed ongoing support gap.
Technically substantial, longitudinal multi-channel design if built with real care.
weaknesses: No way to validate against real population data at hackathon scale, must be honest about this limitation.
Real risk of the check-in itself feeling surveillant or re-traumatizing if tone and design aren't handled with real care.

roles_needed: Conversational/engagement design person (tone is critical here)
Someone explicitly responsible for escalation-safety design
team_fit.ideal_ratio: Same as SIH26093, every team member should understand and share responsibility for the human-safety framing, this isn't a technical feature to delegate.
team_fit.approach: Design the check-in tone and escalation pathway before any modeling work, get this right first.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard check-in scheduling/messaging infrastructure and basic sentiment/trend analysis scaffolding.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Every decision about check-in tone, cadence, consent design, and escalation triggering, this is fundamentally a human-safety and care-design problem.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI system generating check-in messages or interpreting distress trends without careful human design oversight risks producing something that feels clinical, intrusive, or that mishandles a genuine escalating crisis, real, serious consequences, not hypothetical ones.

data_resource_availability.status: No real victim data should be used; general longitudinal mental-health monitoring research can inform design responsibly, but population-specific validation requires real oversight beyond hackathon scope.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Use clearly synthetic, appropriately-constructed test scenarios for demonstration, and be explicit that real deployment requires genuine clinical and ethical validation.

judge_qna.question: How do you prevent this check-in system from feeling surveillant or adding to someone's distress rather than helping?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific design choices, opt-in/opt-out control, warm non-clinical tone, respect for the person's autonomy over engagement, and be honest this is a genuine design risk you took seriously, not an afterthought.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would a victim actually consent to and control their ongoing participation in this monitoring?

judge_qna.question: What happens the moment your system detects a genuinely escalating crisis?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your immediate, unambiguous human-escalation pathway explicitly, this should be the most concrete, well-thought-through part of your entire system, not a vague 'alert sent' gesture.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your system's behavior if the person doesn't respond to a check-in at all, could silence itself be a concerning signal?
